claims: General Motors is facing a 2026 class action lawsuit.
The lawsuit alleges that 2023–2026 Cadillac Lyriq electric SUVs suffer from critical defects in their electrical, software, and battery management systems.
The lawsuit alleges that the Lyriq's electrical architecture and battery management systems fail, rendering the car useless and requiring towing.
The lawsuit alleges that these defects can cause the vehicle to become inoperable or "bricked," often leaving it unable to start, charge, or operate.
Many plaintiffs report that dealerships are unable to promptly repair the vehicles, leaving owners without their cars for weeks or months.
The complaint alleges that GM was aware of these issues through pre-release testing, customer complaints, and dealer repair reports.
The complaint alleges that GM continued to market the vehicle.
The suit was filed in Washington state on April 2, 2026.
The suit seeks class action status on behalf of all affected owners nationwide.
Some complaints highlight issues with the vehicle’s one-pedal driving (OPD) and braking systems.
Numerous individuals are pursuing "lemon law" claims for compensation due to recurring electrical issues that cannot be repaired.
The suit notes that GM has offered to buy back some defective Lyriq vehicles.
Reports indicate that some owners have faced long wait times for parts.
Reports indicate that in some cases, serious issues have required total battery replacements.
